html:
A set of treaties signed in 1648 in the towns of Osnabrück and Münster, in Westphalia, that ended the Thirty Years' War in the Holy Roman Empire and the Eighty Years' War between Spain and the Dutch.

The Thirty Years' War began in 1618 as a fight between Catholic and Protestant states in the empire and grew into a European war. Armies from Sweden, France, Spain and the emperor fought across German lands, and disease and hunger killed a large share of the people.

What the peace settled:

  • Spain recognised the independence of the Dutch Republic.
  • Switzerland's independence from the empire was accepted.
  • Each prince in the empire could choose Catholic, Lutheran or Calvinist faith for his land, and the princes gained more freedom from the emperor.
  • France and Sweden gained territory.

The congress was the first great peace meeting of many European states. Later writers saw in it the start of a system of sovereign states that do not interfere in each other's affairs, Westphalian sovereignty. Historians argue how much the treaties themselves meant that.
sum: A set of treaties signed in 1648 in the towns of Osnabrück and Münster, in Westphalia, that ended the Thirty Years' War in the Holy Roman Empire and the Eighty Years' War between Spain and the Dutch.
